De overeenkomst dient daarom ruimte te bieden voor op- en afschalen van capaciteit en expertise. Tilaaja katsoo lisä- ja muutostyöksi vain lopullisen toteutuksen suunnitelmamuutokset. Kaikista väliaikaisista ratkaisuista ja niiden aiheuttamista kustannuksista vastaa urakoitsija. Urakkamuoto tukee hankkeen tehokasta johtamista sekä aikataulun, kustannusten ja laadun hallintaa. title: Finland – Tomography devices – SPET-TT laitteisto
description: Etelä-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjoustanne SPET-TT laitteistosta oheisen hankintaohjelman ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Hankintaohjelma kaikkine liitteineen on kiinteä osa tarjouspyyntöä. Hankinnan kohteena on uusi kaksidetektorinen yleiskäyttöinen SPET-TT -yhdistelmälaite, joka soveltuu isotooppilääketieteen perustutkimuksiin ja jossa on diagnostisiin TT-kuvauksiin soveltuva TT-laitteisto, jossa aksiaalikuvauksessa laitteisto pystyy mittaamaan vähintään 32 leikettä/pyörähdys. Laitteiston tulee muodostaa toimintavalmis kokonaisuus, johon sisältyvät kuvaus-, rekonstruktio-, fuusio-, laadunvalvonta-, käyttökoulutus-, huolto- ja vastaanottotarkastuskokonaisuudet. Laitteen tulee täyttää kaikki lainsäädännön ja viranomaisvaatimusten asettamat vaatimukset. Laitteisto hankitaan Seinäjoen keskussairaalan Fysiologian ja isotooppitutkimusten yksikköön. Kuvauslaitteiston tulee soveltua planaari- ja koko kehon kuvauksiin, dynaamisiin kuvauksiin, SPET- ja SPET-TT -kuvauksiin, elliptisen/non circular-pyörähdysten ja potilaan ääriviivoja seuraaviin kuvauksiin, EKG-tahdistetuihin ja kaksoisisotooppikuvauksiin, luuston, munuaistoiminnan, sydänperfuusion, sydämenoikovirtauksen, keuhkojen perfuusion ja ventilaation, vartijaimusolmukkeiden, lisäkilpirauhasen, kilpirauhasmetastaasien ja aivojen dopamiinitransportterien gammakuvauksiin. description: Ordregiver udbyder herved rammeaftale om tandreguleringsbehandlinger og retentionsforløb for børn og unge i Dragør Kommune, som er omfattet af Sundhedsstyrelsens kriterier for et kommunalt ortodontisk behandlingstilbud. Derudover kan der på rammeaftalen købes retentionsfremstilling og kontrol af disse. De omfattede behandlinger er inddelt i fire kategorier og nærmere beskrevet i udbudsmaterialets Bilag 2: Kravspecifikation. Ordregiver forventer at henvise ca. 100-120 patienter årligt, men tallet kan variere i både op- og nedadgående retning. Estimatet på 100-120 patienter årligt er et vejledende tal baseret på årgangsstørrelse, forventet forekomst af behandlingskrævende tandstillingsafvigelser samt erfaringer fra tidligere år. Leverandørerne er dog ikke garanteret nogen minimumsmængde af bestillinger. Leverandøren skal dog acceptere at modtage minimum 5 patienter pr. måned og i alt minimum 55 patienter årligt. Der forventes ingen henvisninger i juli måned. Ved aftalens indgåelse er der ophobet en mindre pulje af patienter, der er visiteret af Ordregiver i fjerde kvartal 2026 samt januar 2027 (ca. 10 patienter pr. måned), hvorfor der forventes henvisning af flere patienter ved kontraktopstart, forudsat at leverandøren/leverandørerne kan modtage patienterne. Klinikkerne, hvorpå behandlingen foregår, skal være fysisk beliggende i Danmark og inden for maksimalt 50 km fra Dragør Rådhus, målt som den korteste mulige rute kørt med bil. Afstandsbegrænsningen er begrundet i hensynet til transporttid og transportomkostninger for patienterne. Baggrunden for at ydelserne skal leveres i Danmark er, at der arbejdes efter dansk sundhedslovgivning. Ordregiver vil indgå rammeaftale med de (op til) tre leverandører, som samlet set har afgivet de økonomisk mest fordelagtige tilbud på tværs af de fire prissatte behandlinger i kategori 1-4. title: Ireland – Astronomical and optical instruments – Procurement of a High-Precision Optical Ground Station (OGS) Telescope Unit for Uplink and Satellite Tracking
description: The Contracting Authority is seeking tenders for the procurement of a High-Precision Optical Ground Station (OGS) Telescope Unit for Uplink and Satellite Tracking. This procurement is being undertaken as part of Phase 2 of Ireland's QCI project (TransEuroOGS), co-funded by the European Commission Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) and the Irish Department of Culture, Communications, and Sport. The successful tenderer will be required to design, manufacture, and deliver a turnkey telescope unit encompassing the mount, optics, and control software, complying with strict technical and spatial constraints. Key Technical Requirements: Optical Configuration: Ritchey-Chretien (RC) optical design, f/10 to f/12 system, with a clear aperture of at least 700 mm. Low central obstruction is required (30 percent or lower diameter linear obstruction preferred, maximum allowable 34 percent or lower). Optical Coatings and Power Handling: Broad-spectrum reflectivity covering both visible wavelengths and the 1550 nm C-Band NIR telecommunication spectrum, biased for optimal performance at 1550 nm. Reflectance at 1550 nm must be at least 95 percent (protected gold or equivalent high-efficiency NIR coating acceptable). The secondary mirror (M2) and main aperture must handle a high-power launch beam of maximum 40W continuous wave at 1550 nm across the aperture or annulus (power density less than 3300 W per square metre on the primary mirror). Focusing Path and Clear Aperture: Must feature at least one Nasmyth focus port (more preferred). The Nasmyth focus path must be completely free of refracting optical elements (100 percent reflective optics only, with removable optics as an allowable deviation). Clear aperture path through the Nasmyth axis must be at least 60 mm diameter to support downstream Adaptive Optics relay systems. Mount and Dynamic Tracking Specifications: Alt-Azimuth Direct-Drive or equivalent performance mount with low-latency tracking dynamics supporting Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite tracking, including high-elevation passes over Zenith. Minimum Azimuth Slew Rate must be at least 5 degrees per second (faster preferred). Pointing and tracking accuracy must be less than 8 to 10 arcsec RMS during dynamic LEO passes. Fastest tracking rate must exceed 1 degree per second with fine range control below this speed. Envelope and Enclosure Compatibility: Total vertical height must not exceed 3000 mm from the base to ensure dome clearance. Maximum radial swing clearance envelope must be at most 1470 mm. The axis of elevation pivot height must ensure clearance at all pointing directions, with the pivot axis positioned no more than 155 mm below the centre of the clearance envelope (or at the centre or higher). Full CAD models and opto-mechanical layout files are mandatory upon contract award. Software, Control Interface and API: Native integration with standard open-source astronomical communication protocols (INDI / INDIGO) or ASCOM / ALPACA frameworks. Open, fully documented network API adaptable to HTTP/REST or WebSocket interfaces for automated robotic control, telemetry, and scriptable trajectory loading. Ethernet data interface and DC power supply preferred. Delivery Constraint: Unit delivery must be completed within 3 to 4 months maximum from contract signature. Please refer to the detailed Technical Specification document for full technical specifications, compliance matrices, and contractual terms.

title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: Clathrate Therapeutics Platform
description: This technology from scientists at Los Alamos National Laboratory represents a novel platform for improving the safety and effectiveness of therapeutic gas-based treatments by enabling controlled, localized delivery at the site of disease. By addressing longstanding challenges associated with systemic exposure and dosing precision, the platform enhances the clinical viability of gas therapies across high-value markets such as oncology, cardiovascular care, and regenerative medicine. In addition, the inclusion of a complementary predictive modeling capability supports treatment optimization and development efficiency, reducing technical risk and accelerating translation. Together, these capabilities position the technology as a differentiated and scalable solution that can unlock new commercial opportunities in areas where gas-based therapeutics have shown promise but faced delivery limitations. The Opportunity: Therapeutic gases have demonstrated meaningful biological effects across oncology, cardiovascular disease, neuroprotection and regenerative medicine, yet their clinical adoption has been limited by a fundamental challenge: safe, controlled and localized delivery. Existing approaches often result in rapid release, systemic exposure or narrow therapeutic windows, creating safety, regulatory and development barriers. The Clathrate Therapeutics Platform addresses this unmet need by positioning gas-based therapies as programmable, targetable and commercially viable treatment modalities. By enabling more precise control over where and how therapeutic gases are delivered, the platform has the potential to unlock new product categories, enhance combination treatment strategies and accelerate translation of gas-based therapeutics into high-value clinical markets. How it Works: The Clathrate Therapeutics Platform uses a proprietary, controlled-release system designed to localize therapeutic gases at the intended treatment site rather than allowing them to disperse systemically. This technology temporarily stabilizes the gas within a biocompatible structure that gradually releases it under physiological conditions, enabling sustained and targeted exposure. This controlled release approach is designed to support therapeutic concentrations where needed while limiting circulating levels elsewhere in the body. An integrated computational modeling capability further supports optimization of dosing profiles and treatment parameters, helping guide development decisions prior to in vivo studies. Key Advantages: Localized delivery: Targets therapeutic gases to the intended site while minimizing systemic exposure. Controlled release: Designed for sustained, tunable dosing under physiological conditions. Improved safety margin: Aims to separate therapeutic effect from toxicity risk. Platform versatility: Applicable across oncology, cardiovascular, neurological and regenerative indications. Development optimization: Supported by predictive modeling to guide dose and design decisions. Partnership-ready architecture: Suitable for integration with drug-device combinations and existing treatment modalities. description: The project�s general scope of work is to furnish all tools, equipment, material, permits, labor, supervision, and all other necessary resources to accomplish the following work: This project replaces a portion of the existing campus water loop piping and existing campus water loop isolation valves. The project also includes installing a water booster pump that will be powered by a new equipment branch of emergency power in Building 22. For the new equipment branch of emergency power to be added, new wiring will feed from Building 19 (generator building) utilizing an existing underground conduit to Building 22 to feed a new emergency power distribution panel which will replace the existing emergency power distribution panel that does not meet code requirements. Installation of a new automatic transfer switch and panelboard along with wiring and conduits will be required to create the new equipment branch of emergency power. The project will also disturb many portions of the existing asphalt roadways and parking lots as well as concrete sidewalks and curbing due to excavation work. The contractor shall patch or replace asphalt and concrete as shown on the drawings and repair any areas of the landscaping and lawn that get disturbed during the project. The existing campus water loop piping is located below many of the existing campus roadways and sidewalks, and it is anticipated that most of the new piping will be as well. Therefore, this project shall be completed in phases to allow campus access for employees and Veterans and maintain water service until a tie-in to an existing building service pipe is to take place. If a shutdown of water service for any building is required during the duration of the project, it must be coordinated with the COR. Period of performance is 300 calendar days from receipt of the Notice to Proceed.

description: 18 Nov 2026: Uploaded signed version of Amendment 0002 that updates the RFP. 16 Nov 2026: Q&A responses are posted. An RFP amendment is expected to be posted on 17 Nov 2026. 28 Oct 2026: The TRICARE Medicare Eligible Program Second Generation SAM.gov posting is being updated to reflect a change in proposal due date. The new due date for TMEP2 RFP Proposals is December 03, 2026, at 5.p.m. MST.The DHA anticipates to have responses to questions before receipt of proposals out within the next few weeks. USC Title 10, Chapter 55, and USC Title 32, National Defense, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 199, outline the benefit structure, administrative functions and the various health care programs, including TMEP2. This is a full and open competitive source selection, using best value trade-off procedures in accordance with RFO Federal Acquisition Regulation (RFO FAR) 15.2, Evaluation and Award, as supplemented with Defense FAR Supplement and the DoD Source Selection Procedures (August 2022). The contract awarded will be a Firm Fixed-Price contract. The contract will have a one 12-month base period of transiotion-in activiteis, seven 1-year periods for healthcare delivery, a one 12-month contract period for transition-out activities, and a potential 6-month extension of services permitted per RFO FAR Clause 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services, for a potential total period of performance of 8.5 years.
